statement: Find the point on the curve $y=x^{2}$ that is closest to the point $(3,0)$.
solution:
Let the point be $(x,x^{2})$. The squared distance to $(3,0)$ is $D(x)=(x-3)^{2}+x^{4}$. Differentiating, $D'(x)=2(x-3)+4x^{3}=4x^{3}+2x-6$. Setting $D'(x)=0$: $2x^{3}+x-3=0$. Testing $x=1$ gives $2+1-3=0$, so $x=1$ is a root; the other factors give no real roots. Since $D''(1)>0$, this is a minimum. The closest point is $(1,1)$.
